note: The input must contain at least one byte, which the harness treats as both payload and linktype selector.
The last byte selects the link-layer type for the compiler context, influencing how the filter is optimized.

code: filter = malloc(Size); memcpy(filter, Data, Size); filter[Size-1] = 0;
note: The preceding bytes become the textual filter expression exactly as chosen by the attacker.
The input string is fed to the parser to produce the internal compiler graph and instruction blocks.
The parsed graph is sent into the optimizer, where the reported crash state begins.
Any optimization error unwinds through this setjmp handler and immediately frees optimizer-owned allocations.
After successful optimization, the same cleanup routine runs again on the same state object.
The cleanup routine frees the heap graph; the vulnerability is that the same heap pointer can be released twice along the error/success interaction.
